access_method: Anonymous public HTTPS download from archive.org (no account, no terms accepted, no CAPTCHA, no paywall). The YouTube watch pages were read only for their metadata; nothing was downloaded from YouTube.
rights_holder_best_evidence: Dan Lynch: named as creator on the Internet Archive item, and the owner of the YouTube channel that first published the video (2023-10-14). No document establishes who shot the footage or who holds its copyright.

license_markings_found.applied_by: A third-party uploader account (IA 'uploader' field), which differs from the named creator. The item was uploaded 2025-11-23, and its 'originalurl' points to the creator's YouTube video. The same uploader posted a second creator's footage (Ted Spero, NYC) under CC0 the same day.
license_markings_found.reliance: Not relied on. Nothing shows the uploader owns or was authorized to dedicate the footage, so the CC0 marking is an unsupported claim, not a verified grant.

license_markings_found.marking: No Creative Commons marking on the watch page (the standard YouTube license applies)
license_markings_found.reliance: The standard YouTube license grants no reuse outside YouTube's own service/embedding.

third_party_content_in_frame: The CompUSA name and logo sign: trademark shown incidentally as the subject of a documentary storefront view. The CompUSA brand still exists under later owners.
Unreadable window posters and partly visible passers-by (silhouettes, not identifiable).
not_done: Did not assume public domain or fair use.
Did not contact the creator. That would be a message sent on the user's behalf and needs explicit approval.
Did not remove or obscure the camcorder date stamp (it is part of the original picture and is the date evidence).
review_questions: Seek written permission from Dan Lynch (via the contact route his YouTube channel offers), treat the use as fair use after legal review, or replace the still with a rights-clear later photo such as the CC BY-SA 3.0 Commons image 'CompUSA Santa Clara 2.jpg' (2005), captioned with its real date?
credit_text_if_cleared: Home video: Dan Lynch — Windows 95 'Midnight Madness', CompUSA, Aug. 24, 1995. Via Internet Archive.
